title: The Edge Cases and When to Put the Framework Down
sourceSection: Strategy 19 edge case, Part V closing cluster, and Part VI meta-lessons
keyConcepts: annihilation: close every exit only when decisive advantage exists and repeated harm must be stopped
righteous posture: gain structural advantage from legitimacy, but only if the record can survive scrutiny
one-upmanship: do not rescue a rival who is already defeating themselves
communication: distinguish fair persuasion from manipulation that tries to bypass judgment
inner-front: expose or amplify real contradictions inside a harmful structure
passive-aggression: build hidden leverage under domination, but do not turn evasiveness into a default ethic
chain-reaction: use one ethical dramatic move to force strategic reappraisal without sliding into intimidation
connectingThread: The closing lesson is not how to become dirtier. It is how to recognize the edge-case tools, name their legitimate forms, and know when the strategic frame itself is the wrong frame.
reversalFlags: annihilation overcommits the attacker if decisive advantage is missing
righteous posture collapses on exposed hypocrisy
one-upmanship fails if the rival is not actually self-destructing or keeps causing harm while you wait
communication turns illegitimate when it tries to outrun informed judgment
inner-front slides into subversion when it manufactures contradictions instead of exposing real ones
passive-aggression becomes evasive duplicity when open conflict is possible and fair
chain-reaction loses force when repeated drama becomes the expected pattern
callbackOpportunities: Ch1: self-mastery is still the first and last discipline
Ch3: the best fight is often the one not fought
Ch7 and Ch9: indirect action can be smarter than direct action without becoming a license for manipulation
moralFlagNote: This chapter must state legitimate applications, illegitimate applications, and explicit no-framework zones: intimacy, grief, genuine collaboration, and situations where the other side is not actually an opponent.
